Software Development Romania: An IT Sector Overview

Romania’s software development industry is one of the most promising in Eastern Europe, expanding by 9.46% yearly. Maintaining such steady growth, its market volume will exceed $1.5 billion in 2028.

This country has always been a great place to work as an IT specialist. With over 7,400 IT companies in Romania, it’s natural for many students to choose this field as their major. Accommodating about 117,000 IT experts in 2011, the number of such professionals in Romania has grown to an astonishing 194,000 in 2020 and continues to soar. What was once a sector primarily focused on general programming skills has expanded to diverse IT fields, making the country a hotbed of qualified programmers. PHP, .NET, Python, Lua, and Java are the most popular programming languages here, which also contributes to Romania’s status as the best outsourcing destination.

IT outsourcing in Romania is an optimistic endeavor. The country’s tech export value is over $8 billion, almost twice as much as ten years ago. Such strong positions in the outsourcing market can be explained by the high standards of Romanians when it comes to doing business. Their traditions and attitude towards work, combined with high education and low prices, make the Romanian software development business truly thriving.

Romania’s Employment Conditions

Over the years, there have been significant shifts in Romania’s job environment. There are a wide variety of industries represented in the landscape. Industries such as manufacturing, information technology, agriculture (18.61%), and services (51%). A highly competitive labor market, with a focus on skilled workers, has resulted from this. People with expertise in technology are in high demand.

Employees in Romania often receive their paychecks on the last day of each month. Employees’ monthly paychecks already include employer taxes. Social security, health insurance, and unemployment insurance are all covered by them. These must be paid by employers at the rates specified in the labor code.

Over the past few years, there have been small increases to the minimum wage. The most recent numbers show that the rate is $702/month. Of course, the rate of overtime pay is substantially more than the standard salary, and it is regulated by labor rules!

Health insurance, paid time off, and retirement plans are just a few of the various employee benefits that are typically offered. This is included in their employee benefits as well. Staff satisfaction and retention are both enhanced by these perks.

IT Market in Different Cities Across Romania

If you are about to outsource software development to Romania or just want to explore this country’s IT sector further, learn more about the major IT hubs here first. Several cities largely influence the Romanian tech scene. Let’s look at them one by one and the software developers’ salaries there:

  • Bucharest

The capital city of Romania stands as a prominent tech hub with a burgeoning software developer community. The Romanian Business Journal indicates that this city concentrates two-thirds of the country’s IT market volume. If you aim to outsource software development to Bucharest, note that the IT experts’ salaries range from $40,000 to $45,000 yearly.

  • Cluj-Napoca

Cluj-Napoca, often referred to as the Silicon Valley of Romania, is renowned for its innovation and flourishing IT sector. It houses about 1,300 software development companies Romania and over 15,000 IT experts, as Romania Journal reveals. Owing to the city’s thriving tech ecosystem, software engineers here earn from $33,000 to $37,000 annually.

  • Iași

Iași, the cultural capital of Romania, proves to extend beyond just that. This city has also emerged as a bustling IT and outsourcing hub, with 25% of workers engaged in the IT services sector. The median salary of software engineers in Iași ranges from $27,000 to $32,000 per year.

  • Constanța

Known as a coastal city on the Black Sea, Constanța is making its mark on the Romanian IT map. Beyond excelling in tourist, commercial, and industrial sectors, this city offers favorable software developer jobs and salaries. The IT experts here make $41,000 yearly on average.

  • Timișoara

It’s another vital tech hub in Romania. Notably, only Bucharest and Timișoara made it to the list published by the World Economic Forum, which highlights the cities’ recognition for their innovation. The software engineer salary in Timișoara ranges from $22,000 to $28,000 yearly.

Romanian Developers: What Skills Should They Have?

First of all, you need to know, that Romania is one of the biggest IT talent pools in the whole Eastern Europe – it accounts for nearly 93,000 employees in the field. This means that you will have plenty of specialists to hire Romanian developers. But before you rush to look for that web developer Romania that you need, you have to learn about all the necessary skills he or she must possess. So IT outsourcing Romania specialists must:

  • Have a profile education. Software development is not something that you can master after taking monthly courses, it requires profound knowledge and extensive training. Luckily, IT companies in Romania mostly have programmers with high education what makes one more benefit for custom software development Romania.
  • Experience with back and front end development. Any software developer at some point has to work with either of them and sometimes even switch between them.
  • Have knowledge of such back end development languages as JavaScript, HTML5, PHP, Python, and SQL. You will only benefit if in addition to those IT companies in Romania provide specialists who also know how to operate Node.js.
  • Know how to run and debug his own code if necessary.
  • Be a team player. It is a common myth that software developers are some sort of ‘grumpy loners’ who work alone. In reality, they often need to communicate with one another and the rest of the team members to deliver the best possible result. So, “team-building” in a regular company is not an exception for custom software development company Romania.
  • Have respect for deadlines. Meeting deadlines is a crucial thing in the world of programming as the work of one person often relies on the work of another. So if you want your project to be done in time – make sure your future employee has this trait.
  • Have an impressive portfolio. There is no better way to find out whether or not a software developer is a good match for your team than to look at the examples of his previous work.
  • Be able to take responsibility for his actions and make his own decisions.
  • Be attentive to every little detail as even the slightest mistake in the code can ruin the whole project.

So these are the most important things to look for in your future software developer’s resume. Of course, there is more to the list, however, these are the core ones that will ensure that your specialists will be worth his price.
